findings.diagnosis: The prompt underestimates the harm of cutting inside numeric/measurement/time expressions: splitting percentages, speeds, durations or numeral+unit sequences often creates contradiction or loses core quantity information.
findings.evidence: ['cmn_hans_cn_1413','cmn_hans_cn_242','cmn_hans_cn_1607','cmn_hans_cn_1169']: each case shows a cut that breaks a percent/measurement/time expression and yields high contra or low H.

edit.text: Do not cut inside numeral+unit/measurement/percentage/time/duration/speed expressions; treat the whole numeric expression as an atomic unit for segmentation.

findings.diagnosis: The prompt allows cuts that split multi-character proper names or transliterations, which severs referents and causes contradictions or incoherent fragments.
findings.evidence: ['cmn_hans_cn_1532','cmn_hans_cn_542','cmn_hans_cn_55']: each case shows a policy cut that divides a person/place name or transliterated token and the target keeps the name contiguous.

edit.text: Do not insert cuts inside multi-character named entities or transliterated proper names; keep name characters contiguous so the referent remains recoverable.

findings.diagnosis: When rules forbid verb–complement splits, the prompt sometimes repositions cuts in ways that isolate punctuation or single-character function words; that trade harms short-piece bins.
findings.evidence: ['cmn_hans_cn_1413','cmn_hans_cn_974','cmn_hans_cn_8']: these show punctuation or tiny tokens isolated as standalone pieces after cut moves producing low H or high contra.

edit.text: When preventing verb–object/resultative splits, avoid moves that leave punctuation, quotes, or single-character function words as isolated pieces; attach such tiny tokens to the adjacent phrase they punctuate.
